_chooserLinkTextNote: chooserLinkText is a declared editorial input, not a derived value. It cannot be derived from label or navLabel: four of the seven differ from both (navLabel 'Parent & carer homepage' against 'Open family homepage', and similar for schools, councils and partners). Deriving it would have silently rewritten four visible link texts, so the wording is recorded here - in the file that owns the chooser - rather than left as a literal inside a hand-maintained page. Same class as gameIdOverrides.

studioBand._decision: 2026-08-09: the chooser may carry mailing and support as quiet text links in this band. Ruled by Matt. It replaces a vague 'not dominant' assertion with five precise ones in verify_games_audience_faces.py - text links only, no /account/ or /members/ route on / at all, no price or tier or donate card, the band after the audience section, and reflectMailingFooter with its adultFeaturesAllowed() condition still present. Recorded so nobody restores the old behaviour as a regression.
studioBand._aboutProvenance: Both clauses trace to existing estate copy. 'Made by a teacher, in a real classroom' compresses the Games hub line about teaching in an alternative provision; the second clause compresses main/index.html's own 'lessons, registers and pupil records stay in your browser on your device'. An earlier draft said 'works offline' and 'nothing you do is uploaded' - both were false as written and were not shipped. See BACKLOG 0e.
studioBand.about: Made by a teacher, in a real classroom. Everything here is free to use, and your lessons, registers and pupil records stay on your device.

mainOption._note: /main/ is a homepage type a visitor can choose, and it is deliberately NOT a member of `audiences`. Two reasons, both load-bearing. First, mechanical: outputs() writes ROOT/<route>/index.html for every member of `audiences`, so adding `main` there would render audience_page() straight over the hand-maintained /main/ and destroy it - validate() now rejects that by name rather than leaving it to be discovered. Second, semantic: the seven are audience faces, each with sections, quickLinks, a face accent and a floor on promoted visuals. /main/ has none of those; it is the platform itself. It carries only what a chooser card needs, which is why the record is this short.
mainOption._accentProvenance: Measured, not picked. accent is --mf-navy and soft is --mf-cream: the two brand tokens the estate already owns, so the platform card is painted in the platform's own colours and no new colour is minted. Measurements at 2026-08-10: 16.15:1 on the cream surface and 16.44:1 against white text (bar 4.5:1); nearest audience accent delta-E 40.49 (councils #794390), above the seven's own worst-pair floor of 38.40, so it does not collapse neighbour distinctness. --mf-deep #0F1530 measured better on separation (44.74) and was not chosen: it is the hero ground, not the identity colour. The soft sits delta-E 3.5 from the nearest existing soft (councils #F1E3D2), above the seven softs' own floor of 2.78. check_audience_accents.py re-measures all of this on every run.
mainOption._linkTextNote: chooserLinkText plays the same role it plays for the seven - the visible text of the link that opens this homepage from another homepage. For an audience that link sits on /main/; for /main/ it sits in the switcher at the foot of each audience homepage. Its wording is the literal that switcher() carried before this record existed, adopted unchanged so retiring the literal changed no visible copy and no served byte.
